item.title: ElectricSQL vs PowerSync vs Triplit in 2026: Which Local-First Sync Engine Should You Build On?
item.description: Offline support is not a feature you add at the end. It is a data-architecture decision, and by the time a product manager asks for “offline mode”, the answer is usually already locked in by how you fetch and mutate data. That is why local-first sync engines exist: they replace hand-rolled cache invalidation with a replication protocol that keeps a client-side database in step with Postgres.

item.title: Self-Hosted Hospital Management for Low-Resource Settings: HospitalRun vs OpenMRS vs Bahmni
item.description: In low-resource healthcare settings — rural clinics in sub-Saharan Africa, mobile medical units serving refugee camps, island hospitals with intermittent satellite internet — traditional cloud-dependent hospital management software is fundamentally unusable. These environments require systems that operate fully offline, synchronize when connectivity is available, and run on modest hardware that can be powered by solar panels and batteries. The offline-first architecture isn’t a feature checkbox; it’s an operational necessity when a clinic’s internet connection might be unavailable for days or weeks at a time.
